name: planning-skills-for-agents-and-humans
description: Planning workflows with evidence-gated Lead User research, fluid collaborative shaping, explicit promotion gates, Wayfinding, breadboarding, executable handoffs, context, and reflection.

interface.displayName: Planning Skills for Agents and Humans
interface.shortDescription: Research future needs, shape fluidly, gate commitment, and build bounded slices.
interface.longDescription: Reusable workflows that help humans and agents investigate future-facing needs with evidence-gated Lead User research; start planning from requirements, a solution idea, evidence, or a focused uncertainty; preserve explicit human promotion gates; and hand bounded accepted context to implementation.
defaultPrompt: Use the shaping skill in collaborative mode. Start from whatever is already most concrete—requirements, a proposed solution, a prototype, current-system evidence, or a focused unknown—and move among R, S, fit checks, spikes, sketches, and candidate breadboards as useful. Keep Working material separate from Accepted intent and do not select for me.
Use the planning-router skill to choose the smallest next move without forcing a fixed exploration order.
Use the framing-doc skill when raw evidence, notes, or requests need a clear problem, desired outcome, and boundary before shaping.
Use the shaping skill in S-first mode to capture my solution idea as a candidate shape, extract provisional requirements from it, and refine both without selecting automatically.
Use the shaping skill to run a focused spike and return explicit implications to R, S, fit, and Appetite.

Use the breadboarding skill in candidate-shape mode to clarify one named candidate uncertainty; provisional requirements or Appetite are allowed in collaborative mode but must be labeled and cannot support final selection by themselves.
Use the gated/orchestrated profile when I explicitly ask for strict prerequisites and stop at every human promotion gate.
Use the wayfinding skill to coordinate this bounded multi-session planning effort as dependent decision, evidence, prototype, and prerequisite tickets.
Use the sketch-reconciliation skill to map an attached sketch or screenshot to planning IDs and propose explicit deltas without silently changing accepted scope.
Use the breadboarding skill in selected-design mode only after a shape is explicitly selected and the judging inputs are accepted.
Use the statechart skill only when a selected stateful portion of an accepted breadboard needs a transition table and behavioral projection.
Use the interface-contracts skill to define plain-language contracts for the selected slice boundaries.
Use the executable-breadboards skill to add examples, fixtures, expected outputs, edge cases, and acceptance tests before implementation.
Use the dumplink skill when a selected project needs vertical task groups with dependency-aware sequence, risk states, or scope cuts.
Use the feed-planning-context skill to package only accepted authoritative context for an implementation agent.
Use the breadboard-reflection skill to compare accepted intent with implementation reality and prepare an explicit correction decision.
Use the kickoff-doc skill when builders need a durable orientation reference derived from accepted planning artifacts.

Use the lead-user-research skill when the decision depends on future-facing needs. Start or resume from persisted state, perform only the next valid phase, use real evidence with exact citations and privacy controls, and stop for explicit acceptance before research implications feed framing.
